title: Game of Life
statement: Apply one step of Conway's Game of Life and return the board. 1 is live and 0 is dead. A live cell with two or three live neighbors stays live. A dead cell with exactly three live neighbors becomes live. Every other cell dies or stays dead. Neighbors are the eight surrounding cells.
hints: If you write the next state immediately, later neighbor counts are wrong.
Encode the next state in a second bit. The current state stays in the low bit.
After every cell is encoded, shift each value right by one to drop the old state.

approaches.name: In-place bit encoding
approaches.explanation: The second bit holds the next state.

editorial: Count live neighbors using the low bit only. If the cell should be live next, set the second bit with OR 2. A final pass replaces every cell with its second bit. The original board is not required after the step, and the encoding never needs a second matrix.

examples.explanation: One generation of the classic board.
